reply_text:
㊥ Gist: Elephant-2000 already has most of what we need. Agents can post a structured offer, and when you type plain "yes" in the REPL it is recorded as an agreement, through a parser in Emacs and a matching one on the server. Your "🈸:yes" was read as ordinary text, though, because the parser only knows "yes", "yes 2" and "yes act:ID 2". I've posted an offer for the next decision so you can try it. Type "yes 1" to make "🈸:yes" count as a spelling of yes, or "yes 2" to keep plain yes and have agents post an offer behind each 🈸.

㊢ (what P11 already does, all in futon3c)
- **Offers:** an agent posts `POST /api/alpha/offer` with numbered options. The record is stored with the agent's seat and its permission to make offers, and your prompt line shows it as pending.
- **Acceptance:** what you type goes through `agent-chat--acceptance-command` in Emacs and `parse-acceptance` in `agreement_record.clj`, which use the same rules. A recognised yes is posted to `/api/alpha/agreement`, which stores an agreement naming the offer, the option and your turn. Your buffer gets a "yes: agreement …" line.
- **Ambiguity:** a bare yes with more than one open offer isn't taken as acceptance. The agent is told to ask which one.
- **What it leads to:** per the design, agreements feed the record of who owes what (P9).

㊩ (what "🈸:yes" did) Nothing was recorded, for two reasons. I hadn't posted an offer for that question, so there was nothing to accept. And "🈸:yes" doesn't match either parser, which only accept text starting with "yes". So for P11, the gap between the marks and the records is the agent side: a 🈸 in a reply currently creates no offer.

㊢ (the offer now open) `act:c7b94af3-b8bd-4947-b064-6c22853d90eb`, open until 3 October:
1. Accept "🈸:yes" (and "🈸:yes 2") as a spelling of yes in both parsers, with tests. That is a two-file change. P11 asked for exact matching on fixed strings and no reading of agent text by a language model, and this keeps both.
2. Make no parser change. Agents post an offer for each 🈸, and you answer with plain yes. This needs only a line in CLAUDE.md's reply-proforma section.

Either way, agents will need to post the offer whenever they write a 🈸. That is the step that connects the marks to Elephant-2000. Any 🈸 without an offer gives you nothing to agree to.

🈸 (one decision) Reply "yes 1" or "yes 2". Your buffer should then show a "yes: agreement" line, which would also confirm the whole path works.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: C-c ; works in your buffer now. Your claude-17 REPL runs on its own copy of the key map, made before these bindings existed, so binding the mode map didn't reach it. The fix also binds the keys in any open REPL buffer like that (commit 1ee5fea7), and I checked that in *claude-repl:claude-17* C-c ; and C-c x p now run the right commands. I agree about the ledger and am dropping it: the marks should feed Elephant-2000's records, not a new store.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the key was missing) Every other Claude REPL buffer already had C-c ;. Yours didn't even have C-a, which the current mode map binds, so it was clearly running on an older map. Loading the file now binds the keys in such buffers too.
